clue_checks.clue: I was the first woman.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 2:22 describes God making a woman from the man's rib, the first woman in the narrative. Genesis 3:20 identifies this woman as Eve.

clue_checks.clue: I was made from a rib taken from the man.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 2:22 states that the woman was made from the rib the LORD God had taken from man.

clue_checks.clue: The serpent spoke to me in the garden.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 3:1 records the serpent speaking to the woman about the trees of the garden. Context identifies her as Eve.

clue_checks.clue: I am called the mother of all living.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 3:20 says Adam named her Eve because she was the mother of all living.

clue_checks.clue: My father was Laban.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:16 names Rachel as Laban's younger daughter. The clue also fits Leah, but that is acceptable because it is an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: Jacob served seven years for me, and they seemed but a few days.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:20 says this almost word for word.

clue_checks.clue: I was the mother of Joseph and Benjamin.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 35:24 lists Joseph and Benjamin as the sons of Rachel.

clue_checks.clue: I died on the way to Bethlehem.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 35:19 says Rachel died and was buried in the way to Ephrath, which is Beth-lehem. The clue is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I am called a soothsayer.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 13:22 calls 'Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer.'

clue_checks.clue: Balak, king of Moab, sent for me to curse Israel.
clue_checks.reason: Verses 5-6 show messengers sent to Balaam to curse the people. The sender is only 'He', identified as Balak son of Zippor, king of the Moabites, in verse 4. The clue is accurate in context, but the quoted text alone does not name Balak or Moab. Citing Numbers 22:4-6 would be more exact.

clue_checks.clue: An angel with a drawn sword stood in my way.
clue_checks.reason: Numbers 22:31 says Balaam saw the angel of the LORD standing in the way with his sword drawn in his hand.

clue_checks.clue: My ass spoke to me.
clue_checks.reason: Numbers 22:28 says the LORD opened the mouth of the ass and she spoke to Balaam.

clue_checks.clue: I was a Levite and the brother of Moses.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 4:14 calls him 'Aaron the Levite thy brother', said to Moses.

clue_checks.clue: I spoke to Pharaoh on Moses' behalf.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 7:2 says 'Aaron thy brother shall speak unto Pharaoh', conveying what God commanded Moses.

clue_checks.clue: I made a golden calf when the people asked.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 32:1-4 says the people asked Aaron to make gods. He collected golden earrings and made a molten calf, so 'golden calf' is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: My rod budded and yielded almonds.
clue_checks.reason: Numbers 17:8 says the rod of Aaron budded, bloomed blossoms and yielded almonds.

clue_checks.clue: I was Abram's nephew.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 12:5 calls Lot 'his brother's son,' meaning Abram's nephew. None of the other options fits: Terah is Abram's father, Nahor is his brother, and Laban is Nahor's grandson.

clue_checks.clue: I chose all the plain of Jordan.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 13:11 says 'Lot chose him all the plain of Jordan.'

clue_checks.clue: Two angels came to my house in Sodom.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 19:1-3 says two angels came to Sodom, and Lot brought them into his house.

clue_checks.clue: My wife looked back and became a pillar of salt.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 19:26 says 'his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt'. The surrounding verses (19:23) make clear 'his' refers to Lot.

clue_checks.clue: I drew water for a stranger's camels at a well.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 24:19-20 shows Rebekah offering to draw water and drawing for all the servant's camels at the well.

clue_checks.clue: I was the sister of Laban.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 24:29 states Rebekah had a brother named Laban. Rachel and Leah were Laban's daughters, not his sisters.

clue_checks.clue: I married Isaac.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 24:67 states Isaac took Rebekah and she became his wife.

clue_checks.clue: I helped my son Jacob receive his father's blessing.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 27:6-17 shows Rebekah instructing Jacob, preparing the meat, and disguising him so that he would receive Isaac's blessing.

clue_checks.clue: My mother laughed when my birth was promised.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 18:12 says Sarah laughed within herself at the promise of a son. Isaac is not named in the verse, but the surrounding context (18:10-14) makes the son Isaac.

clue_checks.clue: My father was a hundred years old when I was born.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 21:5 says Abraham was an hundred years old when his son Isaac was born unto him.

clue_checks.clue: I was laid on an altar in the land of Moriah.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 22:9 says Abraham bound Isaac and laid him on the altar. The verse itself does not mention Moriah, which comes from Genesis 22:2.

clue_checks.clue: My sons were Esau and Jacob.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 25:25-26 names Esau and Jacob and says Isaac was threescore years old when she bare them, identifying Isaac as their father.

clue_checks.clue: I was a priest of Midian.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 3:1 calls Jethro 'the priest of Midian.'

clue_checks.clue: I was Moses' father-in-law.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 18:1 calls Jethro 'Moses' father in law.'

clue_checks.clue: Moses kept my flock near Horeb.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 3:1 says Moses kept Jethro's flock and led it to Horeb, the mountain of God. 'Near Horeb' is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I advised Moses to appoint rulers to judge the people.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 18:21-22 gives the advice to appoint rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens to judge the people. The surrounding context (18:17) identifies the speaker as Moses' father-in-law.

clue_checks.clue: I was the wife of Uriah the Hittite.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 11:3 identifies Bath-sheba as 'the wife of Uriah the Hittite.'

clue_checks.clue: King David saw me washing as he walked on his roof.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 11:2 says David walked upon the roof of the king's house and from the roof saw a woman washing herself. Verse 3 identifies her as Bath-sheba.

clue_checks.clue: I became the mother of Solomon.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 12:24 says Bath-sheba bare a son, and he called his name Solomon.

clue_checks.clue: My son King Solomon set a seat for me at his right hand.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 2:19 says Solomon caused a seat to be set for the king's mother, and she sat on his right hand.

clue_checks.clue: I was a prophet in David's court.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 7:2 shows the king speaking with 'Nathan the prophet' at his house of cedar. Gad also fits this clue, but that is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: I told David his son would build God's house.
clue_checks.reason: In 2 Samuel 7:12-13 God promises that David's seed 'shall build an house for my name.' The context (7:4, 7:17) shows Nathan delivered this word to David.

clue_checks.clue: I told David a parable about a poor man's ewe lamb.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 12:1-4 has the LORD sending Nathan, who tells the parable of the rich man and the poor man's one little ewe lamb.

clue_checks.clue: I said to David, Thou art the man.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 12:7 states it verbatim: 'And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a son of King David.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 3:3 names Absalom as the third of the sons born to David in Hebron. Verse 2 makes the context explicit.

clue_checks.clue: I stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
clue_checks.reason: The verse quotes this nearly verbatim of Absalom.

clue_checks.clue: I led a rebellion against my father.
clue_checks.reason: The passage describes Absalom's conspiracy: being proclaimed king in Hebron and drawing away David's counsellor. In context, this is a rebellion against David.

clue_checks.clue: My head caught in an oak as my mule went on.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 18:9 states his head caught hold of the oak and the mule went away.

clue_checks.clue: I was a champion of the Philistines.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 17:4 says a champion went out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath.

clue_checks.clue: I came from Gath.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 17:4 identifies him as 'Goliath, of Gath.' Achish was also of Gath, but the later clues rule him out.

clue_checks.clue: My height was six cubits and a span.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 17:4 states his height was six cubits and a span.

clue_checks.clue: A shepherd boy struck me down with a sling and a stone.
clue_checks.reason: 17:49-50 confirms that David slew the Philistine with a sling and a stone, but the cited text does not call David a shepherd boy. That detail comes from elsewhere in the chapter (17:15, 17:34 keeping sheep; 17:42 'but a youth').

clue_checks.clue: I was the son of King Saul.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 14:49 names Jonathan first among Saul's sons. Ishbosheth was also Saul's son, but this is only an early clue, and later clues exclude him.

clue_checks.clue: I climbed up to a Philistine garrison with my armourbearer.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 14:13 says Jonathan climbed up with his armourbearer after him. The 'garrison of the Philistines' is named in the surrounding context (14:11-12), not in verse 13 itself. The paraphrase is accurate to the context.

clue_checks.clue: My soul was knit with the soul of David.
clue_checks.reason: Nearly verbatim from 1 Samuel 18:1.

clue_checks.clue: I warned David by shooting arrows.
clue_checks.reason: In 1 Samuel 20:36-37 Jonathan shoots the arrows and cries 'Is not the arrow beyond thee?', which is the agreed warning sign (cf. 20:22).

clue_checks.clue: I was the daughter of the king of the Zidonians.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 16:31 calls Jezebel 'the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians.'

clue_checks.clue: I was the wife of King Ahab.
clue_checks.reason: In 1 Kings 16:31 Ahab 'took to wife Jezebel'; context (v.30) identifies him as Ahab.

clue_checks.clue: I threatened Elijah's life after Mount Carmel.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 19:1-2: after Ahab reported the slaying of the prophets, Jezebel sent a messenger vowing to make Elijah's life like theirs by tomorrow.

clue_checks.clue: I arranged Naboth's death to take his vineyard.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 21:7-15: Jezebel wrote letters arranging false witnesses and Naboth's stoning, then told Ahab to take possession of the vineyard.

clue_checks.clue: I was a priest at Shiloh.
clue_checks.reason: The verse places the scene in Shiloh and calls Eli 'the priest' sitting by a post of the temple of the LORD there.

clue_checks.clue: I thought Hannah was drunken as she prayed.
clue_checks.reason: The verse states directly that 'Eli thought she had been drunken.'

clue_checks.clue: My sons Hophni and Phinehas were wicked.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 2:12 calls Eli's sons 'sons of Belial' but does not name them. The names Hophni and Phinehas appear in 1 Samuel 1:3 (and 2:34, 4:11).

clue_checks.clue: I fell backward and died when I heard the ark was taken.
clue_checks.reason: 4:18 says he fell backward and died when the ark of God was mentioned. That the ark was taken is stated in 4:17, and Eli is named in 4:16. In context the clue is accurate.

clue_checks.clue: I was a king of Israel.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 16:29 states Ahab reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty and two years. The clue also fits the other options, but that is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: I married Jezebel.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 16:31 says he took to wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal. The 'he' refers to Ahab from the preceding verses.

clue_checks.clue: I asked Elijah, Art thou he that troubleth Israel?
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 18:17 quotes Ahab saying exactly this to Elijah.

clue_checks.clue: I wanted Naboth's vineyard for a garden of herbs.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 21:2 records Ahab asking Naboth for his vineyard so that he may have it for a garden of herbs.

clue_checks.clue: I was a king of Judah.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 18:1 says Hezekiah son of Ahaz king of Judah began to reign. This clue also fits all the other options, which is acceptable for an opening clue.

clue_checks.clue: I broke in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 18:4 states he 'brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made.' This is unique to Hezekiah.

clue_checks.clue: Isaiah told me to set my house in order.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 20:1 records Isaiah saying to the sick Hezekiah, 'Set thine house in order.'

clue_checks.clue: God added fifteen years to my life.
clue_checks.reason: Isaiah 38:5 has the LORD saying, 'I will add unto thy days fifteen years.' 2 Kings 20:6 parallels this. The past-tense paraphrase is fine.

clue_checks.clue: I became king of Judah at eight years old.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 22:1 states Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign in Jerusalem. Joash, the closest distractor, was seven (2 Kings 11:21).

clue_checks.clue: The book of the law was found in the temple in my reign.
clue_checks.reason: Hilkiah found the book of the law 'in the house of the LORD.' Verse 3 of the same chapter places this in the eighteenth year of king Josiah, so it was in his reign.

clue_checks.clue: I rent my clothes when it was read to me.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 22:11 says the king rent his clothes on hearing the words of the book. In context (22:3-10) the king is Josiah, and the book was read before him (22:10).

clue_checks.clue: I kept a great passover.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 23:21-23 describes an unprecedented passover held in Josiah's eighteenth year. Hezekiah also kept a great passover (2 Chronicles 30), but the earlier clues rule him out.

clue_checks.clue: I was a priest and a ready scribe in the law of Moses.
clue_checks.reason: Ezra 7:6 calls Ezra 'a ready scribe in the law of Moses' but does not call him a priest. His priesthood is stated elsewhere, for example Ezra 7:11 ('Ezra the priest, the scribe') and Nehemiah 8:2, and is implied by the Aaronic lineage in Ezra 7:1-5. The cited text alone does not support the 'priest' part.

clue_checks.clue: I went up from Babylon in the reign of Artaxerxes.
clue_checks.reason: Ezra 7:1 places this 'in the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia', and 7:6 says 'This Ezra went up from Babylon.' Nehemiah also served under Artaxerxes, but he came from Shushan, so the clue fits Ezra specifically.

clue_checks.clue: I read the book of the law to the people.
clue_checks.reason: Nehemiah 8:2-3 says Ezra the priest brought the law before the congregation and read therein from morning until midday.

clue_checks.clue: I stood upon a pulpit of wood.
clue_checks.reason: Nehemiah 8:4 says 'Ezra the scribe stood upon a pulpit of wood.'

clue_checks.clue: I was among the herdmen of Tekoa.
clue_checks.reason: Amos 1:1 says Amos 'was among the herdmen of Tekoa.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a gatherer of sycomore fruit.
clue_checks.reason: In Amos 7:14 Amos says 'I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit.'

clue_checks.clue: I said I was no prophet, neither a prophet's son.
clue_checks.reason: Amos 7:14 has 'I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet's son.'

clue_checks.clue: I cried: let judgment run down as waters.
clue_checks.reason: Amos 5:24 is part of the oracle Amos proclaimed. 'Cried' is acceptable paraphrase for his prophetic declaration.

clue_checks.clue: I was a priest of the course of Abia.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:5 names Zacharias as a priest of the course of Abia.

clue_checks.clue: An angel appeared to me by the altar of incense.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:11 says an angel of the Lord appeared to him standing on the right side of the altar of incense.

clue_checks.clue: I was struck dumb because I did not believe.
clue_checks.reason: In Luke 1:20 the angel tells him he will be dumb because he believed not; this fairly paraphrases the verse.

clue_checks.clue: I wrote: His name is John.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:63 quotes his written words exactly.

clue_checks.clue: I was a priest among the captives by the river Chebar.
clue_checks.reason: Ezekiel 1:3 names Ezekiel the priest in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar. The phrase 'among the captives' comes from Ezekiel 1:1, not the cited verse, but it is accurate.

clue_checks.clue: I saw wheels whose rings were full of eyes.
clue_checks.reason: Ezekiel 1:18 says the rings were full of eyes. In context (1:15-16) the rings belong to the wheels.

clue_checks.clue: I lay on my side for many days as a sign.
clue_checks.reason: Ezekiel 4:4-6 has God command Ezekiel to lie on his left side 390 days and his right side 40 days, each day for a year. This is a fair paraphrase; the word 'sign' appears in the immediate context (4:3).

clue_checks.clue: I prophesied to a valley of dry bones.
clue_checks.reason: Ezekiel 37:1-4 sets Ezekiel in the valley of very dry bones and commands him to prophesy to them. His obedience follows in 37:7, so the clue is accurate.

clue_checks.clue: I was a prophet to Israel.
clue_checks.reason: Hosea 1:1-2 says the word of the LORD came to Hosea in the days of Jeroboam, king of Israel, and addresses the land's whoredom. Amos also fits this clue, but an early clue may fit another option.

clue_checks.clue: I obeyed God and took Gomer as my wife.
clue_checks.reason: Hosea 1:2-3: God commands him to take a wife, and 'So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim.'

clue_checks.clue: I named a son Loammi.
clue_checks.reason: Hosea 1:9 records God commanding Hosea, 'Call his name Lo-ammi.' The context (1:8) is a son born to Gomer. Saying Hosea named him is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I bought a woman for fifteen pieces of silver and barley.
clue_checks.reason: Hosea 3:2: 'So I bought her to me for fifteen pieces of silver, and for an homer of barley, and an half homer of barley.' The first-person narrator is Hosea.

clue_checks.clue: I was of the daughters of Aaron.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:5 says Zacharias's wife 'was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth.'

clue_checks.clue: I was barren and well stricken in years.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:7 says Elisabeth was barren and that they both were well stricken in years.

clue_checks.clue: My babe leaped in my womb when Mary greeted me.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:41 says that when Elisabeth heard Mary's salutation, the babe leaped in her womb.

clue_checks.clue: I was the mother of John the Baptist.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:57-60 shows Elisabeth bore a son and insisted he be called John. The title 'the Baptist' does not appear in this passage, though the identification is sound from the wider narrative.

clue_checks.clue: I was a prophetess of the tribe of Aser.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:36 calls Anna 'a prophetess... of the tribe of Aser.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a widow of about fourscore and four years.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:37 uses this wording: 'a widow of about fourscore and four years.'

clue_checks.clue: I served God with fastings and prayers night and day.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:37 says she 'served God with fastings and prayers night and day.'

clue_checks.clue: I gave thanks when the child Jesus was brought to the temple.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:38 says she gave thanks 'in that instant.' The detail that the child was brought to the temple comes from the surrounding context (Luke 2:27), not from verse 38 itself. This is an accurate contextual paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I was a just and devout man in Jerusalem.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:25 states that Simeon was a man in Jerusalem who was 'just and devout.'

clue_checks.clue: The Holy Ghost revealed I would not die before seeing the Lord's Christ.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:26 says the Holy Ghost revealed that he should not see death before he had seen the Lord's Christ.

clue_checks.clue: I took the child Jesus up in my arms in the temple.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:28 supports taking the child up in his arms, but the temple setting comes from Luke 2:27, not 2:28. The detail is accurate but not in the cited verse.

clue_checks.clue: I said: Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace.
clue_checks.reason: This matches Luke 2:29 verbatim.

clue_checks.clue: I was from Bethsaida.
clue_checks.reason: John 1:44 states Philip was of Bethsaida. Andrew was also from Bethsaida, but this is an early clue and later clues distinguish Philip.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus said to me, Follow me.
clue_checks.reason: John 1:43 says Jesus found Philip and said, Follow me.

clue_checks.clue: I told Nathanael: Come and see.
clue_checks.reason: John 1:46 has Philip saying 'Come and see' to Nathanael.

clue_checks.clue: I asked Jesus: Lord, shew us the Father.
clue_checks.reason: John 14:8 quotes Philip saying exactly this.

clue_checks.clue: I was from Cana of Galilee.
clue_checks.reason: John 21:2 names "Nathanael of Cana in Galilee."

clue_checks.clue: I asked: Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?
clue_checks.reason: John 1:46 records Nathanael asking exactly this.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus saw me under the fig tree.
clue_checks.reason: In John 1:48 Jesus says, "when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee."

clue_checks.clue: Jesus called me an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile.
clue_checks.reason: John 1:47 quotes this verbatim about Nathanael.

clue_checks.clue: I was of the house and lineage of David.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:4 states Joseph 'was of the house and lineage of David.'

clue_checks.clue: An angel told me in a dream not to fear to take Mary as my wife.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 1:20: the angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream saying 'fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife.'

clue_checks.clue: I took the young child and his mother into Egypt by night.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 2:14 says 'he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt.' The context (2:13) shows 'he' is Joseph.

clue_checks.clue: People called Jesus the carpenter's son.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 13:55 records people asking 'Is not this the carpenter's son? is not his mother called Mary?' This identifies Mary's husband, Joseph, as the carpenter.

clue_checks.clue: I was the Roman governor of Judaea.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 3:1 says 'Pontius Pilate being governor of Judæa.' Felix was also a governor, but this early clue is narrowed down by the later ones.

clue_checks.clue: My wife sent word about a dream concerning a just man.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 27:19 says his wife sent word about 'that just man' because of a dream. The context (27:17) identifies 'he' as Pilate.

clue_checks.clue: I asked: What is truth?
clue_checks.reason: John 18:38 has Pilate saying, 'What is truth?'

clue_checks.clue: I washed my hands before the multitude.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 27:24 says Pilate 'took water, and washed his hands before the multitude.'

clue_checks.clue: I was high priest that same year.
clue_checks.reason: John 11:49 names Caiaphas as 'the high priest that same year.' Annas is also called high priest elsewhere (Luke 3:2; Acts 4:6), but this is an early clue, and the later clues rule him out.

clue_checks.clue: I said it was expedient that one man should die for the people.
clue_checks.reason: John 11:50 continues Caiaphas's words from v.49: 'it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people.'

clue_checks.clue: Annas was my father-in-law.
clue_checks.reason: John 18:13 says Annas 'was father in law to Caiaphas.'

clue_checks.clue: Annas sent Jesus to me bound.
clue_checks.reason: John 18:24: 'Annas had sent him bound unto Caiaphas the high priest.'

clue_checks.clue: I lived in Joppa.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:36 states 'there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha.'

clue_checks.clue: I was full of good works and almsdeeds.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:36 says 'this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did.'

clue_checks.clue: I made coats and garments that the widows showed.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:39 describes the widows 'shewing the coats and garments which Dorcas made.'

clue_checks.clue: Peter said to me, arise, and I opened my eyes.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:40 records Peter saying 'Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eyes.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a Pharisee and a doctor of the law.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 5:34 explicitly calls Gamaliel 'a Pharisee' and 'a doctor of the law.' Nicodemus was also a Pharisee, but this is only the first clue, so that overlap is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I was had in reputation among all the people.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 5:34 says Gamaliel was 'had in reputation among all the people.'

clue_checks.clue: I told the council to let the apostles alone.
clue_checks.reason: In Acts 5:38 Gamaliel tells the council 'Refrain from these men, and let them alone,' referring to the apostles. The context in Acts 5:34-35 shows he was addressing the council.

clue_checks.clue: Paul was brought up at my feet.
clue_checks.reason: In Acts 22:3 Paul says he was 'brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel.'

clue_checks.clue: I was from Bethsaida.
clue_checks.reason: John 1:44 calls Bethsaida 'the city of Andrew and Peter.' This clue alone also fits Philip, but that is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: I first heard John the Baptist speak about Jesus.
clue_checks.reason: John 1:40 says Andrew was 'one of the two which heard John speak, and followed him.' The word 'first' adds a claim the text does not make: it implies Andrew was the first to hear, when the text only says he was one of two hearers.

clue_checks.clue: I brought my brother Simon to Jesus.
clue_checks.reason: John 1:41-42 says he found his brother Simon and 'brought him to Jesus.'

clue_checks.clue: I told Jesus of a lad with five barley loaves.
clue_checks.reason: John 6:8-9 names Andrew as the one who said, 'There is a lad here, which hath five barley loaves.'

suggested_fix: Reword clue 2 to 'I was one of two who heard John the Baptist speak and followed Jesus.' The explanation says Andrew 'brought him to Jesus,' but that wording is in John 1:42, outside the cited John 1:40-41. Change the reference_label to John 1:40-42 and add verse 42's 'And he brought him to Jesus' to ref_kjv. Alternatively, shorten the explanation to match verses 40-41.

clue_checks.clue: I was a Jew born at Alexandria.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 18:24 calls Apollos 'a certain Jew' who was 'born at Alexandria.'

clue_checks.clue: I was an eloquent man, mighty in the scriptures.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 18:24 uses this exact wording for Apollos.

clue_checks.clue: Aquila and Priscilla taught me the way of God more perfectly.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 18:26 says Aquila and Priscilla 'expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.' 'Taught' is a fair paraphrase. It also rules out Aquila as the answer.

clue_checks.clue: Paul wrote that he planted and I watered.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Corinthians 3:6 reads 'I have planted, Apollos watered.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a centurion of the Italian band.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 10:1 calls Cornelius 'a centurion of the band called the Italian band.' Julius was a centurion too, but of 'Augustus' band' (Acts 27:1), so this clue is distinctive.

clue_checks.clue: I was a devout man who prayed to God alway.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 10:2 says he was 'a devout man... and prayed to God alway.'

clue_checks.clue: An angel told me to send to Joppa for Peter.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 10:3-5 has an angel tell Cornelius to 'send men to Joppa, and call for one Simon, whose surname is Peter.'

clue_checks.clue: The Holy Ghost fell on all who heard Peter speak in my house.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 10:44 confirms the Holy Ghost fell on all who heard the word. It does not mention 'my house'; that setting comes from the context (Acts 10:24-27), where Peter enters Cornelius's house. The clue is accurate, but the cited verse alone does not show the location.

clue_checks.clue: My husband Aquila and I were tentmakers.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 18:3 says 'by their occupation they were tentmakers.' The husband-wife relationship comes from the preceding verse (18:2, 'his wife Priscilla'), which the item also cites.

clue_checks.clue: We came from Italy when Claudius commanded the Jews to leave Rome.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 18:2 says Aquila was 'lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:)'.

clue_checks.clue: Paul stayed and worked with us in Corinth.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 18:3 confirms that Paul 'abode with them, and wrought.' However, the location Corinth is named in Acts 18:1, not in the cited verse.

clue_checks.clue: We expounded the way of God more perfectly to Apollos.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 18:26 states that Aquila and Priscilla 'expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.'

clue_checks.clue: I was king in Judaea when Jesus was born.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 2:1 places Jesus' birth in Bethlehem of Judaea 'in the days of Herod the king.'

clue_checks.clue: I was troubled when wise men asked for the King of the Jews.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 2:3 says Herod the king was troubled on hearing 'these things,' which refers to the wise men's question in 2:2.

clue_checks.clue: I told the wise men to bring me word again.
clue_checks.reason: In Matthew 2:8 the speaker is Herod (from context in 2:7), and he tells them to 'bring me word again.'

clue_checks.clue: I ordered the children in Bethlehem slain.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 2:16 says Herod 'sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a chief man among the brethren.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 15:22 names 'Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, chief men among the brethren.'

clue_checks.clue: I travelled with Paul after he parted from Barnabas.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 15:40 shows Paul choosing Silas and departing. The parting from Barnabas is in Acts 15:39, which is not quoted, though the context makes it clear.

clue_checks.clue: I was beaten and put in the stocks with Paul at Philippi.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 16:22-24 describes the beating and the stocks but refers only to 'them'. Paul and Silas are named in Acts 16:19, and the setting at Philippi is given in Acts 16:12, neither of which is quoted. The clue is accurate in context.

clue_checks.clue: At midnight Paul and I prayed and sang praises.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 16:25 explicitly names Paul and Silas praying and singing praises at midnight.

clue_checks.clue: I lived in the valley of Sorek.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 16:4 describes Delilah as 'a woman in the valley of Sorek', which reasonably supports that she lived there.

clue_checks.clue: The lords of the Philistines offered me silver.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 16:5 says each lord promised her eleven hundred pieces of silver.

clue_checks.clue: I asked a strong man the secret of his strength.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 16:6 records Delilah asking Samson wherein his great strength lay.

clue_checks.clue: I had his seven locks shaved while he slept.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 16:19 says she made him sleep on her knees and called a man to shave off the seven locks of his head.

clue_checks.clue: My husband Nabal was churlish.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 25:3 names Nabal as Abigail's husband and says he 'was churlish and evil in his doings.'

clue_checks.clue: I brought bread, wine and figs to David's men.
clue_checks.reason: Verse 18 lists loaves, wine and cakes of figs. It does not say who received them. Verse 27 says the gift was for 'the young men that follow my lord,' but that verse is not in the quoted text. This is a minor gap.

clue_checks.clue: I persuaded David not to shed blood.
clue_checks.reason: In 25:33 David blesses her advice, which 'hast kept me this day from coming to shed blood.'

clue_checks.clue: After Nabal died, I became David's wife.
clue_checks.reason: 25:39-42 records that David heard Nabal was dead, sent for Abigail, and she 'became his wife.'

clue_checks.clue: I was the wife of Heber the Kenite.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:17 names 'Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite.'

clue_checks.clue: Sisera fled to my tent.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:17 says Sisera 'fled away on his feet to the tent of Jael.'

clue_checks.clue: I gave him milk when he asked for water.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:19: he asked for 'a little water' and she 'opened a bottle of milk, and gave him drink.'

clue_checks.clue: I drove a nail of the tent into his temples.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:21: Jael 'took a nail of the tent... and smote the nail into his temples.'
